stands._src: Zale, Nov 24 15:30: About holds only what no other page covers. Experiences live on Home and The Farm, discovery on Home and the Lineup, press quotes on Home. The three commitments are Zale's Nov 23 direction (a community festival; sustainable for everyone; good for artists, mutual benefit). Facts: KBOO 1999 (Festival History 9), dishes 2011 and Treeline 2017 to the veterans village (Festival History 8), more than once (Festival History), Will Oldham quote (Press source of truth, SPIN 2025). Words are drafts for Copy Review.

r.t: Built by the people who show up
r.x: It began as a benefit for KBOO community radio. Volunteers still run much of it, and students and makers build the neighborhoods.
r.alt: The Cherry Hill neighborhood, built by students

r.x: Real plates and steel cups since 2011. Every structure is built for a second life: the 2017 Treeline stage now shelters veterans.
r.alt: Hands washing a reusable plate beside a steel cup

r.t: Good for the people on stage
r.x: Most artists play more than once, so nobody rushes. “A respect for humanity that is absent in the makeup of most festivals.” Will Oldham, in SPIN
r.alt: Rogê playing in the middle of the Woods crowd

eras.x: Four eras. Every year has its own poster.

r.x: A one-day benefit for KBOO, run by volunteers.
Pendarvis Farm becomes home, and students start building the stages.
No festival in 2020 or 2021, then back in 2022 as neighborhoods.
A 10-year permit, and Creative Neighborhoods starts building to last.
